title: Alabama transition landscape: installations, TAP delivery, state programs, oversight findings
scope_note: Factual content only. Market sizing, pitch framing and 'investable insight' language from the landscape report are excluded under CLAUDE.md (no sales or investor work). Statistics live in statistics.json; disagreements in conflicts.json.

installations.name: Maxwell-Gunter AFB
installations.role: Air University, PME (Air War College, ACSC, SOS, CCAF)
installations.tap_delivery: Full TAP at 42d Force Support Squadron Airman & Family Readiness Center (Bldg 677); five-day workshop. SkillBridge applications moved into AFVEC on 2025-06-26.

installations.name: Redstone Arsenal
installations.role: AMC, MDA, NASA Marshall, FBI HQ-South
installations.tap_delivery: Virtual-only SFL-TAP since 2025-05-12; was a volunteer-supported satellite, never a funded center. In-person fallback is Fort Rucker (334-255-2558); 50+ miles away use the SFL-TAP Virtual Center (1-800-325-4715).

installations.name: Fort Rucker (formerly Fort Novosel)
installations.role: U.S. Army Aviation Center of Excellence
installations.tap_delivery: Only fully resourced contractor-staffed SFL-TAP center in Alabama; primary live node after the Redstone change. Heavy warrant-officer and aviator flow; strong SkillBridge use.

redesignation.authority: Department of the Army General Orders 2025-18

installations.name: Anniston Army Depot
installations.role: Tracked combat vehicles and small arms (mostly civilian workforce)
installations.tap_delivery: No full TAP center; Virtual Center, or travel to Fort Rucker, Fort Moore (GA) or Fort Campbell (KY). GAO small/remote-installation profile.

installations.name: USCG Aviation Training Center Mobile
installations.tap_delivery: Coast Guard TAP; still implementing FY19 NDAA counseling pathways as of late 2023.

guard_reserve_note: Alabama Army and Air National Guard members route through the Yellow Ribbon Reintegration Program and demobilization-site TAP.

state_programs.name: Alabama Department of Veterans Affairs (ADVA)
state_programs.detail: About $230M total budget including federal pass-through and trust funds; $175.6M tracked state appropriation in FY2025 ($5.08M General Fund + $170.5M earmarked). 62 county Veterans Service Offices (12 added in the past 36 months per source). Main line (334) 242-5077.

state_programs.name: Alabama Veterans Resource Center (AVRC)
state_programs.detail: Public corporation created by Senate Bill 70 (2025) with a $5M initial appropriation, located in Montgomery; board appointments announced July 2025. Designed to fill the state flagship-program gap.

state_programs.name: Alabama G.I. Dependents' Scholarship
state_programs.detail: HB284 (2024) raised the cap from $250 to $400 per credit hour effective 2024-07-31. See state_benefits sb.AL.gi_dependents.

state_programs.name: State veterans homes
state_programs.detail: Five homes (~700+ beds). CSM Bennie G. Adkins State Veterans Home in Enterprise opened September 2024 (~$115M federal-state cost share).

state_programs.name: Jobs for Veterans State Grant staffing (Alabama Career Centers)
state_programs.detail: 21 DVOP specialists, 12 LVERs, 3 Consolidated Outreach and Development Liaisons; $2.5–4M JVSG per year (estimate).

state_programs.name: Homeless Veterans Reintegration Program grantees
state_programs.detail: Aletheia House (Birmingham, Montgomery); Volunteers of America Southeast (Mobile Eagle's Landing, Tuscaloosa Valor Grove); typically $300K–$500K per grantee per year.

state_programs.name: Workforce Alabama job portal and ADOL DVOP/LVER specialists
state_programs.detail: Above-federal-floor service without a branded state transition flagship.

state_programs.name: Heroes Welcome Initiative (interstate licensure compact participation)
state_programs.detail: Named as the lever for military-spouse licensing; links to reciprocity gap CB-06.

state_programs.name: No state veteran home-loan program
state_programs.detail: Alabama veterans rely on the federal VA loan (contrast Texas VLB, CalVet, Wisconsin trust fund).

peer_flagships.name: Virginia Values Veterans (V3)
peer_flagships.detail: Codified employer certification (Code of VA § 2.2-2001.2) with transition teams at installations.

peer_flagships.name: Veterans Florida
peer_flagships.detail: State-authorized nonprofit integrating SkillBridge, entrepreneurship and a career portal.

peer_flagships.name: Texas Veterans Commission + GLO Veterans Land Board
peer_flagships.detail: 170+ employment reps in 75+ cities; Hazlewood; College Credit for Heroes; Operation Welcome Home.

peer_flagships.name: NC4ME
peer_flagships.detail: Public-private partnership with NCWorks priority postings and 50 veteran specialists.

peer_flagships.name: Operation Palmetto Employment
peer_flagships.detail: Tiered veteran-friendly employer recognition; SC Smart Start virtual platform.

peer_flagships.name: CalTAP
peer_flagships.detail: 23-module state curriculum, online and in eight regional centers.

peer_flagships.name: STRONG Act / Helping Heroes Grant
peer_flagships.detail: Named by the TAP report as Tennessee's state program.

tap_structure.start_requirement: TAP must begin no later than 365 days before separation.
tap_structure.counseling_tiers: Individualized Initial Counseling assigns Tier 1 (minimum), Tier 2 (moderate), Tier 3 (maximum; mandatory two-day track).
core_curriculum: VA Benefits and Services (Briefings I and II; no exemption permitted)
DOL Employment Fundamentals of Career Transition
tap_structure.capstone: Capstone verification at least 90 days before separation.

oversight_findings.finding: 70% of separating members did not start TAP at least one year out; about 25% of Tier 3 members skipped the mandatory two-day class; services waived the two-day class for 53% of members.
4,300 required warm handovers to VA, DOL or SBA not delivered (Apr 2021–Mar 2023); one-third of ~41,000 logged handovers unverified; 77,711 members verified by commanders with no recorded handover.
inTransition did not connect with over 70% of eligible members it identified in 2022.
All five suicide-prevention recommendations for transitioning members still open as of January 2024.
Of $14.3B federal transition spending in FY2019 only $140M went to TAP; raw analysis associates TAP participation with lower wages, attributed mainly to selection effects.

oversight_findings.citation: Penn State Clearinghouse evaluation of IVMF Onward to Opportunity (2022)
oversight_findings.finding: Only rigorously evaluated transition program found; positive effects on starting salary and six-month retention.

oversight_findings.citation: Blue Star Families Military Family Lifestyle Survey 2024
oversight_findings.finding: 28% of veterans used TAP and found it helpful, 23% used it and did not, 49% did not use it; 54% who found useful resources found them through peers.

62% began TAP less than a year out; one-third did not get or did not know about required community-resource connections; nearly one-third did not know their tier; 15%+ of spouses could not attend or did not know they could.
Veterans' main hurdle is finding reliable resources.

what_works: SBA Boots to Business: 241,000+ graduates since 2013; 91% of veteran-founded businesses operating after one year (per SBA as cited).
VA Benefits Briefings I and II: 94–96% satisfaction historically.
DoD SkillBridge: 12,000+ enrolled in Q1–Q2 FY2024; 3,000+ partner organizations.
DAV Transition Service Officers: 38 TSOs at 109+ installations; 39,000+ members assisted in 2024.
VA Solid Start: permanent under the Solid Start Act of 2022 (Pub. L. 117-205); contacted 71% of eligible veterans in 2021.

policy_timeline.event: FY2019 NDAA TAP reforms take effect (Pub. L. 115-232 §552): tiers, counselor meetings, self-assessment, 365-day start.
DoD Military-Civilian Transition Office created (TVPO + Office of Reintegration Programs).
Isakson-Roe Act §4303 (Pub. L. 116-315) authorizes DOL Off-Base Transition Training pilot; no Alabama site; five-year authority sunsetting absent reauthorization.
Solid Start Act of 2022 (Pub. L. 117-205) makes VA Solid Start permanent.
FY2024 NDAA (Pub. L. 118-31) adds TAP accountability and SkillBridge oversight.
HB284: Alabama G.I. Dependents' Scholarship cap $250 → $400 per credit hour.
CSM Bennie G. Adkins State Veterans Home opens in Enterprise.
SB70 creates the Alabama Veterans Resource Center with $5M.
Air Force SkillBridge applications move into AFVEC.

product_implications: Start the transition clock at 365+ days: most members start TAP late, so the Mission Brief should surface TAP timing as a first-five action.
Spouses are routinely excluded from TAP; spouse_family is already a transition track and should get its own brief.
Warm handovers fail silently; the closed-loop referral state machine (Plane 2) is the countermeasure.
Rural installations (Fort Rucker, Anniston) and the Redstone virtual shift raise the value of a digital state layer.

First-year post-separation suicide risk is about 2.5x the active-duty rate and inTransition misses 70%+: the crisis floor must be on every screen (already true) and the crisis detector (R16) is a priority once agents exist.
